statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). CME equity index futures are in the daily maintenance halt between 21:00 and 22:00 UTC, so no tradable price path can form in the current hour. The final Nasdaq-100 futures print was 29,489.75, down 0.66%, in the upper part of a 29,107.25 to 29,604.50 range after an opening gap to 28,997.75 was largely recovered. The cash index closed at 29,127.16, down 241.28 points or 0.82%, having opened 1.63% below the 29,368.44 previous close and recovered to 29,285.50 before giving part of that back. Both directional legs retraced inside the range, so no persistent one-way structure was established. Cross-asset amplifiers eased into the close: VIX settled at 17.10, up 7.95%, below its 18.17 session high; the 10-year yield closed at 4.961%, negative on the day after trading through 5% to 5.012%; WTI is near 101.89 after a session high around 105. Tail is 16 and maps to the low band.
recommendation: Tail at 16 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is retained at 13:00-15:00 UTC on 15 September, covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where a second consecutive gap open after a chip-led decline on a pre-policy day is the identified conditional risk. The conditional path stays in the low band through the maintenance halt, the Globex reopen, the Asian session and the European morning, with small uplifts at the reopen, the Tokyo open and the European opening auction. It enters the watch band from 12:00 UTC, peaks at 24 at the cash open, eases through the late morning, and steps up again around the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC and into the pre-policy close. Stress remains high at 66 on an unresolved Middle East supply disruption, a 10-year yield that traded through 5%, a semiconductor index down 5.9% on the day, and a policy decision on Wednesday that markets price as a probable 25 basis point increase. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unchanged by this assessment.
headline: Futures halted for the 21:00 UTC maintenance hour after NQ closed at 29,489.75 in the upper part of its range, having recovered most of a 2.3% opening gap; with VIX settling below its 18.17 high and the 10-year closing negative on the day, Tail eases to 16 in the low band
body:
Monday resolved as a two-sided session rather than a directional one, and the current hour removes price-path risk entirely because CME equity index futures are in their daily maintenance halt from 21:00 to 22:00 UTC. Nasdaq-100 futures opened at 28,997.75, roughly 2.3% below the 29,684.25 previous close, traded down to 29,107.25, rallied almost 500 points to a 29,604.50 high and settled at 29,489.75, down 0.66% and only about 115 points off the high. The cash index followed a similar shape, opening 1.63% lower at 28,890.93, bottoming at 28,867.67, recovering to 29,285.50 and closing at 29,127.16, down 0.82%. Both the recovery leg and the late fade retraced inside the range. That is the opposite of the structure that defeats mean reversion, and it is the primary reason Tail eases rather than rises despite a heavy sector decline.

The catalyst was concentrated rather than systemic. Senior figures at several US artificial-intelligence companies called publicly for a slower pace of model development, and the semiconductor complex absorbed most of the damage: the PHLX chip index fell 5.9%, with Nvidia down 3.4% and Broadcom, Micron and Advanced Micro Devices each down more than 4%. The index recovered most of its gap anyway, which indicates the decline was absorbed by rotation rather than transmitted as a broad liquidation. Cross-asset amplifiers also decayed into the close. VIX rose 7.95% to 17.10 but settled well below its 18.17 session high, and the 10-year yield traded through 5% to 5.012%, the first time above that level since 2023, before closing at 4.961% and negative on the day. A reversing yield and a decaying volatility index are both inconsistent with an active tail path.

The standing risks are environmental rather than structural, and they are carried in Stress at 66 rather than in Tail. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut after drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory on 10-11 September, removing the main alternative export route while the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed; WTI is near 101.89 after a session high around 105 and Brent is above 105. This is a chronic, months-old supply condition rather than a fresh discontinuity tonight, which is why it raises the difficulty of the environment without establishing a no-retracement price path. Ahead, the Empire State survey lands at 12:30 UTC on Tuesday and a 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, with the prior stop near 5.204% making it a meaningful checkpoint for the yield channel. The Federal Reserve decision, projections and press conference fall on Wednesday from 18:00 UTC, beyond this forecast window, with market-implied odds around 83% for a 25 basis point increase. The forecast therefore keeps the low band through the overnight and European hours and concentrates conditional risk in a narrow window at the US cash open, where a second consecutive gap open would be the first genuinely observable amplifier.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail moved from 21 at the start of the window to a 26 peak during the European morning decline, repeated 26 at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon to 19 by the cash close as the opening gap was recovered. Stress fell from 79 at its peak to 67, and Confidence held between 74 and 89. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all of them concentrated in the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band through the maintenance halt, the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the Asian session and the European morning, with small uplifts at the reopen, the Tokyo open and the European opening auction. It enters the watch band from 12:00 UTC ahead of the Empire State survey, peaks at 24 across the 13:00-15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and first full cash hour, returns briefly to the low band in the midday lull, then steps up again for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC and the pre-policy close before easing after the cash close. The Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday falls beyond this window.
